identity: Flat, fair, and compared by jockeys to an American dirt track
About 1m2f round, with a home straight of about 3f
5f races (and the 1m6f start) use a straight chute before the final bend
Tapeta, which replaced the old Fibresand surface
1m2f to 1m5f in front of the stands; 6f, 7f and 1m on the back straight
layout: Most races are run on a conventional left-handed oval of about a mile and a quarter, with a run-in of roughly three furlongs after the final turn.
Five-furlong races use a straight course, so they are run without a bend; the 1m6f start also sits on that chute before the runners join the oval.
The final turn is on the tight side by British standards, a little more sweeping than a typical American dirt track.
tactics: With a flat track and a fair surface, few horses are beaten by the course itself; racing position into the final turn can matter on the tighter bends.
Straight 5f races and round-course races call for different things, so read the sprint figures separately from the round-course figures.
Tapeta can ride on the slow side, which can hold times down; a moderate time here is not always a weak performance.
ground: An artificial Tapeta surface, so the going is described as standard, standard to slow or similar rather than good or soft.
The surface changed from Fibresand to Tapeta; ZANS figures here only use races run on Tapeta, so older Fibresand form does not mix in.
guide_note: Course guides describe Tapeta tracks as fair and note that official ratings earned here can come out a few pounds low because times are slower; that is a guide view, not a ZANS measurement.
